notes: PSA 5.4 ng/mL. PI-RADS 2. PSAD 0.14. Prostate volume 38 mL. csPCa 0.73.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prior prostate cancer diagnosis with rising PSA and severe LUTS.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a retired baker living in an assisted-living facility, married, with his brother as next-of-kin. He has osteoarthritis managed with paracetamol PRN and is an ex-smoker (21 pack-yr, quit 2015). Recent appointments include orthopaedic follow-up for knee osteoarthritis, dermatology check for actinic keratosis, and surveillance colonoscopy. He reports severe LUTS (IPSS 27/35) but no haematuria or bone pain. Alcohol-free, exercises with light weight-training twice weekly.
On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without nodules, consistent with cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.
